problem: Object-centric scene-graph memory discards fine-grained visual cues and suffers from detection noise, while existing image-based memories are loosely organized caches with no structure for rooms/frontiers, cause premature stops on same-category objects, and never learn from past successes or failures.
motivation: Zero-shot VLM navigation agents need memory that keeps raw visual evidence yet scales with growing memory and limits costly VLM calls. In lifelong multi-subtask settings, experience from earlier subtasks in the same scene could be reused, but current memories only accumulate without improving.
key_idea: Build a room-view-object Visual-Semantic Memory Graph with raw view images as first-class nodes, navigate it with a budgeted coarse-to-fine policy with multi-view STOP verification, and write back reflection outcomes as training-free graph-attached priors.
insight: The ablation shows budgeted candidate compression (Coarse) is the largest single gain (47.1/30.1 to 58.7/39.7 SR/SPL), while Fine verification helps image goals by curbing premature stops and RDCMA adds a further gain (60.8/40.8 to 64.8/43.1) at negligible cost. Efficiency profiling shows VSMGraph+C2F cuts VLM calls by 41% and graph maintenance time by 58% versus 3D-Mem while improving SR, so structured memory and shortlisting improve both accuracy and cost. RDCMA gains peak in mid subtasks (3-5) as priors accumulate.
method: VSMGraph: room-view-object graph G=(R,V,O,E); view nodes store raw RGB and pose, object nodes store instance hypotheses (YOLOv8-World+SAM cache), navigability and visibility edges, and a CLIP argmax room-type label per view; an occupancy grid is the metric scaffold.

Anchor and frontier views: anchor views are object-rich explored observations used as evidence; frontier views are reachable entry poses of clustered frontier regions with a frontier-facing image, linked to the nearest explored view.

Coarse stage (Explore): room-aware bucketing plus object-hit soft tags compress candidates to budgets K_A and K_F, optionally with a text-only VLM focus hint; an empty anchor set routes to a frontier with no VLM call.

Fine stage (Search + Verify): VLM selects among the shortlist and returns confidence (certain/uncertain/unknown); low-confidence anchor picks are gated back to frontier exploration; on reaching an anchor, multi-view STOP verification returns STOP or RESELECT (RESELECT triggers cooldown).
Recover fallback: on repeated reselect or cooldown deadlock, temporarily enforce frontier-only exploration.

RDCMA: after each subtask, trajectory events and STOP/RESELECT outcomes are written as goal-signature-indexed priors on room/anchor/frontier nodes, with Episode-STM (reset) and Scene-LTM (persistent) and decay, top-K cap and conflict suppression.
Prior usage: priors act as tie-breakers for exploration ordering within bucketed candidates and as a stop-memory hint injected into the verification prompt; no parameter updates.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (frozen) for selection and verification; CLIP for room labels; YOLOv8-World + SAM for instance hypotheses
setting.action_space: graph-level target selection (anchor/frontier view nodes), executed as shortest-path walks on an occupancy grid

results: EvoMemNav reaches 59.6 SR / 38.9 SPL on GOAT-Bench val-unseen, beating the strongest baseline MSGNav (52.0/29.6) and the trained MTU3D (47.2/27.7). On HM3D ObjectNav it gets 59.2/33.6 (v1) and 63.8/39.4 (v2), best SPL and best on v2, while SGM has a higher SR on v1 (60.2).
limitations: The ablation and efficiency analyses use only 36 episodes (one per scene), so the gains are statistically noisy.
Still relies on a detector (YOLOv8-World/SAM) and CLIP for soft cues, and requires posed RGB-D with an occupancy grid; per-episode step counts and token usage increase slightly.
RDCMA relies on the lifelong multi-subtask setting to accumulate priors, so its benefit is limited on single-goal benchmarks and evaluated only in simulation.
